paragraphs: The Buckle, Inc. (the "Company") is a retailer of medium to better-priced casual apparel, footwear, and accessories for fashion-conscious men, women, and kids. As of January 31, 2026, the Company operated 440 retail stores in 42 states throughout the United States under the names "Buckle" and "Buckle Youth." The Company markets a wide selection of casual apparel including denims, other casual bottoms, tops, sportswear, outerwear, accessories, and footwear. The Company emphasizes personalized attention to its customers and provides customer services such as free hemming, free gift-packaging, the Buckle private label credit card, and a guest loyalty program. Most stores are located in regional shopping malls and lifestyle centers. In recent years, however, the Company has successfully relocated several of its stores in smaller and middle markets from enclosed malls into power center locations, with continued plans for pursuing more such relocation opportunities in the future. The majority of the Company's central office functions, including purchasing, pricing, accounting, marketing, and distribution, are controlled from its corporate offices and distribution center in Kearney, Nebraska. The Company's men's buying team is located in Overland Park, Kansas.

Incorporated in Nebraska in 1948, the Company commenced business under the name Mills Clothing, Inc., a conventional men's clothing store with only one location. In 1967, a second store, under the trade name Brass Buckle, was purchased. In the early 1970s, the store image changed to that of a jeans store with a wide selection of denims and shirts. The first branch store was opened in Columbus, Nebraska, in 1976. In 1977, the Company began selling young women's apparel and opened its first mall store. The Company changed its corporate name to The Buckle, Inc. on April 23, 1991 and has experienced significant growth since that time, operating 440 stores in 42 states at the end of fiscal 2025. All references herein to fiscal 2025 refer to the 52-week period ended January 31, 2026. Fiscal 2024 refers to the 52-week period ended February 1, 2025 and fiscal 2023 refers to the 53-week period ended February 3, 2024. All references herein to the "Company", "Buckle", "we", "us", or similar terms refer to The Buckle, Inc. and its subsidiary.

The Company's principal executive offices are located at 2407 West 24th Street, Kearney, Nebraska 68845. The Company's telephone number is (308) 236-8491. The Company publishes its corporate web site at www.buckle.com.

The Company's annual reports on Form 10-K, along with all other reports and amendments filed with or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission, are publicly available free of charge on the Investor Information section of the Company's website at www.buckle.com as soon as reasonably practicable after the Company files such materials with, or furnishes them to, the Securities and Exchange Commission. The Company's corporate governance policies, ethics code, and Board of Directors' committee charters are also posted within this section of the website. The information on the Company's website is not part of this or any other report The Buckle, Inc. files with, or furnishes to, the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Certain statements herein, including anticipated store openings, trends in or expectations regarding the Company's revenue and net earnings growth, comparable store sales growth, cash flow requirements, and capital expenditures, all constitute "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Such statements are based on currently available operating, financial, and competitive information and are subject to various risks and uncertainties. Actual future results and trends may differ materially depending on a variety of factors, including, but not limited to, changes in product mix, changes in fashion trends and/or pricing, competitive factors, general economic conditions, economic conditions in the retail apparel industry, successful execution of internal performance and expansion plans, and other risks detailed herein and in the Company's other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

A forward-looking statement is neither a prediction nor a guarantee of future events or circumstances, and those future events or circumstances may not occur. Users should not place undue reliance on the forward-looking statements, which are accurate only as of the date of this report. The Company is under no obligation to update or revise any forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events, or otherwise.

The Company's merchandising strategy is designed to create loyalty by offering a wide selection of key brand name and private label merchandise and providing a broad range of value-added services. The Company believes it provides a unique specialty apparel store experience with merchandise designed to appeal to the fashion-conscious 15 to 30-year old. The merchandise mix includes denims, casual bottoms, tops, sportswear, outerwear, accessories, and footwear. Denim is a significant contributor to total sales (42.5% of fiscal 2025 net sales) and is a key to the Company's merchandising strategy. The Company believes it attracts guests with its wide selection of branded and private label denim and a wide variety of fits, finishes, sizes, and styles. Tops are also significant contributors to total sales (28.9% of fiscal 2025 net sales). The Company strives to provide a continually changing selection of the latest casual fashions.
The percentage of net sales over the past three fiscal years of the Company's major product lines are set forth in the following table:
2024 Denims 42.5 % 42.5 % 40.9 % Tops (including sweaters) 28.9 29.0 29.3 Accessories 10.9 11.0 10.8
Footwear 4.9 5.3 6.7 Sportswear/fashions 4.8 5.1 5.4 Outerwear 2.2 2.0 2.2 Casual bottoms 1.9 1.5 1.3

Brand name merchandise accounted for approximately 53% of the Company's net sales during fiscal 2025. The remaining balance is comprised of private label merchandise from exclusive brands including BKE, Buckle Black, Ace High, Daytrip, Departwest, FITZ + EDDI, Freshwear, Gentry Country, Gilded Intent, Gimmicks, J.B. Holt, Maven Co-op, Modish Rebel, Nova Industries, Outpost Makers, Reclaim, Salvage, Sterling & Stitch, Veece, Willow & Root, 33 Coastal, and Funk Lagoon. The Company's merchandisers continually work with manufacturers and vendors to produce brand name merchandise, the majority of which they believe is exclusive in terms of color, style, and fit. While the brands offered by the Company change to meet current customer preferences, the Company currently offers denims from brands such as Vervet by Flying Monkey, Hidden, Levi's, Miss Me, Rock Revival, Wrangler, and 7 For All Mankind. Other key brands include Affliction, American Fighter, Ariat, Billabong, Birkenstock, Free People, Goorin Bros., Hey Dude, Hooey, Howitzer, Hurley, K. Swiss, Kimes Ranch, Lost Calf, Mia, Oakley, Old Row, Pendleton, Ray-Ban, Reebok, Ridge, RVCA, SOREL, Steve Madden, Sullen, Very G, White Crow, and Z Supply.

Management believes the Company provides a unique store environment by maintaining a high level of personalized service and by offering a wide selection of fashionable, quality merchandise. The Company believes it is essential to create an enjoyable shopping environment and, in order to fulfill this mission, it employs highly motivated employees who provide personal attention to customers. Each salesperson is educated to help create a complete look for the customer by helping them find the best fits and showing merchandise as coordinating outfits. The Company also incorporates specialized services such as free hemming, free gift-packaging, a guest loyalty program, the Buckle private label credit card, personalized stylist services, and a special order system that allows stores to obtain specifically requested merchandise from other Company stores or from the Company's online order fulfillment center.

Merchandising and pricing decisions are made centrally; however, the Company's distribution system allows for variation in the mix of merchandise distributed to each store. This allows individual store inventories to be tailored to reflect differences in customer buying patterns at various locations. In addition, to ensure a continually fresh look in its stores, the Company ships new merchandise daily to most stores. The Company also has a transfer program that shifts certain merchandise to locations where it is selling best. This distribution and transfer system helps to maintain customer satisfaction by providing in-stock popular items and reducing the need to markdown slow-moving merchandise at a particular location. The Company believes the reduced markdowns justify the incremental distribution costs associated with the transfer system. The Company does not hold store-wide off-price sales at any time.
In management's judgment, the following are material risk factors that might make an investment in the Company speculative or risky:

Dependence on Merchandising/Fashion Sensitivity. The Company's success is largely dependent upon its ability to gauge the fashion tastes of its customers and to provide merchandise that satisfies customer demand in a timely manner. The Company's failure to anticipate, identify, or react appropriately and timely to changes in fashion trends would reduce the Company's net sales and profitability. Misjudgments or unanticipated fashion changes could have a negative impact on the Company's image with its customers, which would also reduce the Company's net sales and profitability.

Dependence on Private Label Merchandise. Sales from private label merchandise accounted for approximately 47% of net sales in both fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024. The Company may increase or decrease the percentage of net sales from private label merchandise in the future. The Company's private label products generally earn a higher margin than branded products. Thus, reductions in the private label mix would decrease the Company's merchandise margins and, as a result, reduce net earnings.

Fluctuations in Comparable Store Net Sales Results. The Company's comparable store net sales results have fluctuated in the past and are expected to continue to fluctuate in the future. A variety of factors affect comparable store sales results, including changes in fashion trends, changes in the Company's merchandise mix, calendar shifts of holiday periods, actions by competitors, weather conditions, and general economic conditions. As a result of these or other factors, the Company's future comparable store sales could decrease, reducing overall net sales and profitability.

Ability to Continue Expansion and Management of Growth. The Company's growth depends on its ability to open and operate stores on a profitable basis and management's ability to manage planned expansion. During fiscal 2026, the Company plans to open 14 new stores. Potential future expansion is dependent upon factors such as the ability to locate and obtain favorable store sites, negotiate acceptable lease terms, obtain necessary merchandise, and hire and train qualified management and other employees. There may be factors outside of the Company's control that affect the ability to expand, including general economic conditions. There is no assurance that the Company will be able to achieve its planned expansion or that future expansion will be profitable. If the Company fails to achieve store growth, there would be less growth in the Company's net sales from new stores and less growth in profitability. If the Company opens unprofitable store locations, there could be a reduction in net earnings, even with the resulting growth in the Company's net sales.

Ability to Adjust to Changes in Shopping Center Traffic and Consumer Trends Related to E-Commerce Shopping. Shopping patterns have been evolving rapidly, along with consumers' ability to shop whenever and wherever they choose. These changing dynamics and increased competition from online retailers have adversely impacted shopping center traffic in many malls. The Company's ability to compete effectively in the future is dependent on its ability to continue to profitably manage both its in-store and e-commerce businesses. The Company considers its unique merchandise selection and its outstanding customer service to be key differentiators. The Company continues to invest in its e-commerce website and other digital initiatives to drive traffic to both its stores and buckle.com. The Company also continues to expand its omni-channel capabilities to satisfy its guests however they choose to shop. There can, however, be no assurance that the Company will be able to successfully integrate both channels and compete successfully with other retailers. The Company's inability to profitably adapt to changing consumer preferences would cause a decrease in the Company's net sales and net earnings.

paragraphs: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and notes thereto of the Company included in this Form 10-K. The following is management's discussion and analysis of certain significant factors which have affected the Company's financial condition and results of operations during the periods included in the accompanying consolidated financial statements included in this Form 10-K.
Company management considers the following items to be key performance indicators in evaluating Company performance.

Comparable Store Sales – Stores are deemed to be comparable stores if they were open in the prior year on the first day of the fiscal period being presented. Stores which have been remodeled, expanded, and/or relocated, but would otherwise be included as comparable stores, are not excluded from the comparable store sales calculation. Online sales are included in comparable store sales. Management considers comparable store sales to be an important indicator of current Company performance, helping leverage certain fixed costs when results are positive. Negative comparable store sales results could reduce net sales and have a negative impact on operating leverage, thus reducing net earnings.

Merchandise Margin – Management evaluates the components of merchandise margin including initial markup and the amount of markdowns during a period. Any inability to obtain acceptable levels of initial markups or any significant increase in the Company's use of markdowns could have an adverse effect on the Company's gross margin and results of operations. Merchandise margin is net sales less merchandise cost of good sold (COGS), as further described in Footnote N, "Segment Reporting".

Operating Margin – Operating margin is a good indicator for management of the Company's success. Operating margin can be positively or negatively affected by comparable store sales, merchandise margins, occupancy costs, and the Company's ability to control operating costs.

Cash Flow and Liquidity (working capital) – Management reviews current cash and short-term investments along with cash flow from operating, investing, and financing activities to determine the Company's short-term cash needs for operations and expansion. The Company believes that existing cash, short-term investments, and operating cash flow will be sufficient to fund current and long-term anticipated capital expenditures and working capital requirements for the next several years.

Net sales for the 52-week fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, increased 6.6% to $1.298 billion from net sales of $1.218 billion for the 52-week fiscal year ended February 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 52-week fiscal year increased 5.6% from comparable store net sales for the prior year 52-week period ended February 1, 2025. The increase in total net sales for the year was the result of a 4.2% increase in the number of transactions and a 3.6% increase in the average unit retail, partially offset by a 1.2% decrease in average number of units sold per transaction. Online sales for the fiscal year increased 9.8% to $217.1 million for the 52-week fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 compared to $197.7 million for the 52-week fiscal year ended February 1, 2025.

The Company's average retail price per piece of merchandise sold increased $1.80, or 3.6%, during fiscal 2025 compared to fiscal 2024. This $1.80 increase was primarily attributable to the following changes (with their corresponding effect on the overall average price per piece): a 3.5% increase in average denim price points ($0.75), a 3.7% increase in average knit shirt price points ($0.42), a 4.2% increase in average accessories price points ($0.23), a 5.9% increase in average footwear price points ($0.14), an increase in average price points for certain other merchandise categories ($0.22), and a shift in the merchandise mix ($0.04). These changes are primarily a reflection of merchandise shifts in terms of brands and product styles, fabrics, details, and finishes.

paragraphs: The Buckle, Inc. (the "Company") 為一家零售中等至較高價位休閒服飾、鞋類及配件的零售商，主要服務時尚意識強的男性、女性及兒童。截至 2026 年 1 月 31 日，本公司於美國 42 個州運營 440 家零售商店，品牌為 "Buckle" 及 "Buckle Youth"。本公司銷售廣泛的休閒服飾，包括牛仔褲、其他休閒下裝、上裝、運動服、外套、配件及鞋類。本公司強調對顧客的個性化服務，並提供如免費縫邊、免費禮盒包裝、The Buckle 自有品牌信用卡及顧客忠誠度計畫等服務。大多數商店位於區域性購物中心及生活方式中心。然而，近年來，本公司已成功將部分商店從封閉式購物中心遷移至強勢購物中心，並持續計畫未來進行更多類似遷移。本公司絕大多數核心辦公室功能，包括採購、定價、會計、行銷及物流，皆由位於內布拉斯加 Kearney 的總部及物流中心控制。本公司男裝採購團隊位於內布拉斯加 Overland Park, Kansas。

本公司於 1948 年在內布拉斯加註冊成立，最初以 Mills Clothing, Inc. 為名營運，為一家僅有單一門市的傳統男裝店。1967 年，本公司購入第二家商店，品牌為 Brass Buckle。1970 年代初期，商店形象轉變為牛仔服飾店，提供廣泛的牛仔褲及襯衫。1976 年，本公司在內布拉斯加 Columbus 開設第一家分店。1977 年，本公司開始銷售年輕女性服飾，並開設第一家購物中心商店。本公司於 1991 年 4 月 23 日將公司名稱改為 The Buckle, Inc.，自那時起經歷顯著成長，截至財務年度 2025 年末，運營 440 家商店，分佈於 42 個州。本文所有提及財務年度 2025 的參考，均指 2026 年 1 月 31 日結束的 52 週財務年度。財務年度 2024 指 2025 年 2 月 1 日結束的 52 週財務年度，財務年度 2023 指 2024 年 2 月 3 日結束的 53 週財務年度。本文所有提及 "Company"、"Buckle"、"we"、"us" 或類似詞彙，均指 The Buckle, Inc. 及其子公司。
本公司主要營業處所位於內布拉斯加 Kearney 的 2407 West 24th Street, Kearney, Nebraska 68845。本公司電話號碼為 (308) 236-8491。本公司網站為 www.buckle.com。

本公司提交的年度報告 10-K 表單，以及所有其他向美國證券交易委員會（Securities and Exchange Commission）提交或提供的報告及更正文件，皆可在本公司網站的投資者資訊區免費取得，於本公司向美國證券交易委員會提交或提供這些資料後盡速公開。本公司企業治理政策、道德準則及董事會委員會章程亦於此網站區內公開。本公司網站的資訊並非本報告或任何其他報告中 The Buckle, Inc. 向美國證券交易委員會提交或提供的資料的一部分。

本文中某些陳述，包括預期商店開幕、服飾產業的趨勢或本公司營業收入及淨利潤成長、同店銷售成長、現金流量需求及資本支出的預期，均屬「前瞻性陳述」，根據 1995 年私人證券訴訟改革法案的定義。這些陳述基於目前可得的營運、財務及競爭資訊，並受各種風險與不確定性影響。實際未來結果及趨勢可能因多種因素而與預期有顯著差異，包括但不限於產品組合的變化、時尚趨勢及/或價格的變化、競爭因素、總體經濟狀況、零售服飾產業的經濟狀況、內部績效及擴張計畫的執行成效，以及其他在本文及本公司其他向美國證券交易委員會提交的資料中詳細說明的風險。
前瞻性陳述並非預測或保證未來事件或情況，且這些未來事件或情況可能不會發生。使用者不應過度依賴前瞻性陳述，這些陳述僅在本報告日為準。本公司無義務更新或修正任何前瞻性陳述，無論是因新資訊、未來事件或其他原因所致。

本公司商品策略旨在透過提供廣泛的知名品牌及自有品牌商品，以及廣泛的附加價值服務，建立忠誠度。本公司認為其提供獨特的專業服飾商店體驗，商品設計以吸引 15 至 30 歲的時尚意識強的顧客為主。商品組合包括牛仔褲、休閒下裝、上裝、運動服、外套、配件及鞋類。牛仔褲是總銷售額的重要組成部分（財務年度 2025 淨銷售額的 42.5%），並為本公司商品策略的關鍵。本公司認為其廣泛的知名品牌及自有品牌牛仔褲選擇，以及多樣的版型、質感、尺寸及風格，能吸引顧客。上裝也是總銷售額的重要組成部分（財務年度 2025 淨銷售額的 28.9%）。本公司致力於提供持續更新的最新休閒時尚商品。
本公司主要產品線過去三年財務年度的淨銷售額佔比，如下表所示：

品牌商品佔本公司淨銷售額約 53% ，於財務年度 2025 。其餘部分則為來自獨家品牌的私標商品，包括 BKE 、 Buckle Black 、 Ace High 、 Daytrip 、 Departwest 、 FITZ + EDDI 、 Freshwear 、 Gentry Country 、 Gilded Intent 、 Gimmicks 、 J.B. Holt 、 Maven Co-op 、 Modish Rebel 、 Nova Industries 、 Outpost Makers 、 Reclaim 、 Salvage 、 Sterling & Stitch 、 Veece 、 Willow & Root 、 33 Coastal 、以及 Funk Lagoon 。本公司買手持續與製造商及供應商合作，生產品牌商品，其中大多數他們認為在顏色、款式及合身度方面為獨家商品。雖然本公司提供的品牌會根據當前顧客偏好而變更，但本公司目前提供牛仔布料商品，包括 Vervet by Flying Monkey 、 Hidden 、 Levi's 、 Miss Me 、 Rock Revival 、 Wrangler 、以及 7 For All Mankind 。其他重要品牌包括 Affliction 、 American Fighter 、 Ariat 、 Billabong 、 Birkenstock 、 Free People 、 Goorin Bros. 、 Hey Dude 、 Hooey 、 Howitzer 、 Hurley 、 K. Swiss 、 Kimes Ranch 、 Lost Calf 、 Mia 、 Oakley 、 Old Row 、 Pendleton 、 Ray-Ban 、 Reebok 、 Ridge 、 RVCA 、 SOREL 、 Steve Madden 、 Sullen 、 Very G 、 White Crow 、以及 Z Supply 。

管理階層認為本公司透過維持高水準的個性化服務，並提供廣泛的時尚、高品質商品，創造獨特的商店環境。本公司認為建立令人愉快的購物環境至關重要，為達成此目標，本公司聘請高度動機的員工，為顧客提供個人化的服務。每位銷售人員皆受過教育訓練，協助顧客打造完整的造型，並協助他們找到最合適的尺碼，並展示商品作為協調的服裝組合。本公司亦提供專門的服務，例如免費縫邊、免費禮品包裝、顧客忠誠度計畫、Buckle 私標信用卡、個人時尚顧問服務，以及特殊訂購系統，讓商店可從其他商店或線上訂單履行中心取得特定需求的商品。

商品管理和定價決策由總部統一進行；然而，本公司之配送系統允許各商店分佈的商品組合有所差異。這使得各商店存貨可根據不同地區顧客的購買新趨勢進行調整。此外，為確保商店內持續呈現新鮮的外觀，本公司每日將新商品運送到大多數商店。本公司亦有商品調撥計畫，將某些商品調撥至銷售表現最佳的地區。此配送與調撥系統有助於維持顧客滿意度，透過提供現貨熱銷商品，並減少特定地區需打折處理銷售緩慢商品的需求。本公司認為減少打折所產生的效益，足以抵消調撥系統所增加的配送成本。本公司不會在任何時間進行全店折扣促銷活動。

paragraphs: 以下討論應與本 Form 10-K 所包含之本公司合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。以下為管理階層對於影響本公司財務狀況及營運成果之重要因素之討論與分析，內容涵蓋本 Form 10-K 所包含之合併財務報表所載期間。
本公司管理階層認為以下項目為評估本公司表現之關鍵績效指標。
可比門市銷售額 – 門市被視為可比門市，若其在財務期間首日為前一財年營運中。即使門市已進行裝修、擴充及/或遷移，但仍符合可比門市條件者，不從可比門市銷售額計算中剔除。線上銷售額包含於可比門市銷售額內。管理階層認為可比門市銷售額為評估本公司當前表現之重要指標，有助於在營運成果為正時支撐部分固定成本。可比門市銷售額為負時，可能降低淨銷售額，並對營運槓桿產生負面影響，進而降低淨收益。
商品毛利 – 管理階層評估商品毛利之組成要素，包括初始加價率及期間內之折扣金額。若無法取得可接受之初始加價率，或本公司使用折扣之金額顯著增加，可能對本公司之毛利率及營運成果產生負面影響。商品毛利為淨銷售額減去商品成本（COGS），如 Footnote N，"應報告分部" 所進一步說明。
營運毛利 – 營運毛利為管理階層評估本公司成功程度之良好指標。營運毛利可能因可比門市銷售額、商品毛利、租金成本及本公司控制營運成本之能力而正向或負向變動。
現金流量與流動性（營運資金） – 管理階層審視現金及短期投資，以及來自營運、投資及融資活動之現金流量，以判斷本公司營運及擴張所需之短期現金需求。本公司認為現有現金、短期投資及營運現金流量將足以支應未來數年內之現有及長期預期資本支出及營運資金需求。
下表列示若干財務資料以淨銷售額百分比表示，並顯示與前一財年比較之金額變動百分比：

本公司於2026年1月31日結息之52週財務年度之淨銷售額，較2025年2月1日結息之52週財務年度之淨銷售額1.218十億美元增加6.6%至1.298十億美元。與前一年度相同店鋪之淨銷售額於2026年1月31日結息之52週財務年度較2025年2月1日結息之52週期間相同店鋪之淨銷售額增加5.6%。全年總淨銷售額之增加係因交易筆數增加4.2%及平均單價零售額增加3.6%，部分抵銷每筆交易平均銷售單位數減少1.2%。財務年度之線上銷售額增加9.8%至2026年1月31日結息之52週財務年度之217.1百萬美元，較2025年2月1日結息之52週財務年度之197.7百萬美元為高。

本公司銷售每件商品的平均零售價格較 2024 年會計年度成長 1.80 美元，或成長 3.6%。此 1.80 美元的成長主要係因以下變動（及其對總平均單價的影響）：平均牛仔布料價格點成長 3.5%（0.75 美元），平均針織襯衫價格點成長 3.7%（0.42 美元），平均配件價格點成長 4.2%（0.23 美元），平均鞋類價格點成長 5.9%（0.14 美元），某些其他商品類別的平均價格點成長（0.22 美元），以及商品組合的變化（0.04 美元）。這些變動主要反映品牌與產品款式、布料、細節與完工度的變化。

paragraphs: 在管理階層的判斷中，以下為可能使投資本公司成為投機或風險因素的重要風險因素：
依賴於商品/時尚敏感度。本公司之成功在很大程度上取決於其能否掌握客戶的時尚品味，並及時提供符合客戶需求的商品。本公司若未能及時預測、識別或適時回應時尚趨勢的變化，將會降低本公司的淨銷售額與利潤。對時尚趨勢的誤判或未預料的時尚變化，可能會對本公司與客戶的聲譽產生負面影響，進而也會降低本公司的淨銷售額與利潤。
依賴於自有品牌商品。自有品牌商品的銷售佔淨銷售額約47% ，於財務年度2025與財務年度2024皆為如此。本公司未來可能增加或減少自有品牌商品佔淨銷售額的百分比。本公司自有品牌產品通常較品牌產品擁有更高的毛利率。因此，自有品牌商品比例的減少將會降低本公司商品的毛利率，進而減少淨利潤。
可比店家淨銷售額結果的波動。本公司的可比店家淨銷售額結果過去曾有波動，並預期未來也會持續有波動。影響可比店家銷售額結果的因素包括時尚趨勢的變化、本公司商品組合的變化、節日期間的曆法變動、競爭對手的行動、天氣條件以及總體經濟狀況。因此，因這些或其他因素，本公司的未來可比店家銷售額可能減少，進而降低總體淨銷售額與利潤。

持續擴張與管理成長的能力。本公司的成長取決於其能否以獲利的方式開設與營運門店，以及管理階層能否有效管理預計的擴張。於財務年度2026，本公司預計將開設14家新門店。未來潛在的擴張取決於諸如能否尋找並取得有利的門店地點、協議可接受的租賃條款、取得必要的商品、以及聘僱與培訓合格的管理及其他員工等因素。可能有某些因素在本公司控制之外，影響擴張的能力，包括總體經濟狀況。本公司無法保證其將能達成預計的擴張，或未來的擴張將是獲利的。若本公司無法達成門店成長，將會導致本公司來自新門店的淨銷售額成長減少，以及利潤成長減少。若本公司開設無利可圖的門店地點，即使淨銷售額因此增加，仍可能導致淨利潤減少。

調整至購物中心人潮與與電子商務購物相關的消費者趨勢的能力。購物模式正在快速演變，同時消費者也能隨時隨地進行購物。這些變動的動態以及來自線上零售商的競爭，已對許多購物中心的人潮產生負面影響。本公司未來能否有效競爭，取決於其能否持續以獲利的方式管理其門店與電子商務業務。本公司認為其獨特的商品選擇與優秀的客戶服務是其關鍵差異點。本公司持續投資於其電子商務網站及其他數位計畫，以吸引流量至其門店與buckle.com。本公司也持續擴展其全渠道能力，以滿足其顧客無論如何選擇購物的需求。然而，本公司無法保證其將能成功整合兩種通路並與其他零售商有效競爭。本公司若無法以獲利的方式適應變動的消費者偏好，將會導致其淨銷售額與淨利潤減少。
